Subject: MAP update + benchmark methodology questions

Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're preparing the MAP sign-off but need the performance artifacts (TTFT/latency at 95/99, throughput under our concurrency profile, and raw run outputs) to attach to procurement. A couple of urgent asks so we can keep toward your proposed Oct close:

- Can you attach the evaluation plan that spells out how you measure TTFT vs token-latency? Our infra team is very prescriptive about load generation and warmup.
- We ran one quick job using our synthetic client and saw TTFTs ~15% higher than your numbers for the same model/seq-length — can you help us triage differences?

If possible, please include a short repro script and a recommended set of client parameters we should run so we can validate locally.

Appreciate it — we want to keep momentum.

Lily Harper

Lily — thanks for the clear list. I've attached an updated MAP (FinLex_MAP_v2.xlsx) and our evaluation plan (redwood_evaluation_plan_v1.pdf). High level summary below and proposed next steps to stay on schedule for a late-October close: 

Summary / what we attached:
- MAP v2: commercial milestones + acceptance criteria. Adds a performance acceptance gate based on 95th/99th latency and TTFT under a 16-worker concurrency profile (your ask).
- Evaluation plan: how we measure TTFT, warmup, batching, and cache-warm/cold behavior. Includes exact client commands, dataset, and metrics collection points.

Proposed immediate plan (owners):
- Neha: run Redwood-side reproductions of your synthetic client profile and share raw CSVs (redwood_bench_results_YYYYMMDD.csv). Target: initial runs by Oct 5.
- Marissa: compile a short competitive comparison appendix if there are signaling differences (e.g., quantization, kernel choices).
- Connor: write a minimal repro script that you can run in your environment.

Timeline:
- Oct 5: Redwood reproductions and first-pass discrepancy notes
- Oct 8: Repro commands and mitigations, small validation with FinLex
- Oct 13: Deep-dive call (2 hours) to walk through logs and align the MAP acceptance gate
- Oct 25: Target internal sign-off at FinLex; Oct 29: final MP execution and procurement handoff (we can shift if critical)

If any of the dates are tight on your side, let us know and we'll adapt.

-Karthik
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-05T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP update + benchmark methodology questions — initial reproduction (attached)

Team / Lily —

Attached are the initial Redwood reproduction runs: redwood_bench_results_20261005.csv (summary + raw samples). Short findings first:

1) Reprobed FinLex profile: we used your described concurrency (16 workers), sequence mix (avg 128 tokens, 10% long-tail 512), and tokenization. Our measured TTFT (median/95/99) matches our public numbers for an empty KV cache, but we do observe a 12–18% delta vs your numbers when we run with the FinLex client stack.

2) Root causes (candidates):
- Client batching: your synthetic client batches requests differently — it applies client-side micro-batching that increases per-request latency under bursty arrival patterns.
- KV cache warmup: your runs appear to include cold-session starts more often; we measure TTFT after an explicit warmup phase and then report steady-state.
- Measurement definition: we measure TTFT as time from POST to first token emitted at the server egress; your client logs measure until first character displayed (which can add client rendering and network buffering).

3) Immediate ask: Connor, can you provide the exact client commands and a tiny script to run on a FinLex box that mirrors our load-generator? If FinLex can run it in their environment, we'll get a side-by-side CSV to pinpoint the delta.

I've left higher-res traces in the CSV and included flags we used for the run (headers at top). Next steps: we plan a small tuning pass (quantization profile and kernel selection) and will surface an appendix for the MAP.

-Neha
Sr. Perf Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MAP update + benchmark methodology questions — repro commands and mitigation suggestions

Lily / Neha —

I've attached a tiny repro sketch (repro_commands_20261008.txt) that mirrors the Redwood load-generator behavior. Key points included in the script:
- Single-request TTFT measurement is taken at client send -> first server token event (server timestamping).
- Explicit 60-second warmup phase before sample collection to prime KV cache and kernels.
- No client-side micro-batching — we leave batching to the server runtime to preserve realistic queuing.

Early hypothesis based on Neha's CSV and our tracing: 
- When client-side micro-batching is enabled it increases queueing variability and shows up as higher TTFT percentiles under bursty arrival patterns.
- If FinLex's environment adds an HTTP proxy or aggressive keepalive re-use in a way that resets connections more frequently, you can see cold-path penalties that look like higher TTFTs.

Mitigations to try (we recommend in this order):
1) Run repro_commands_20261008.txt as-is in your cluster (should take ~30 minutes).
2) If delta persists, switch off client micro-batching and re-run.
3) If cold-starts are the issue, add a short steady-state warmup (60s) to the MAP acceptance gate.

Connor O'Brien
Perf Tools Lead | Redwood Inference

We accept the MAP v2 acceptance gate with the small change: add an explicit 60s warmup clause to the performance acceptance criteria (per Connor's suggestion). We've attached the signed MAP page (FinLex_MAP_approved_signature.pdf).

Please schedule the Oct 13 deep-dive for 11:00–13:00 PT. We'll have our infra leads and procurement present. Given the additional validation, we need the final procurement handoff by Oct 29. If you foresee any blocking items that would stop that, flag them.
